notes:
I don't have any research notes on Song of Solomon 4 for you this time. My tool limit ran out before a single page loaded. My first attempt tried to fetch eight sources at once, and the search tool stopped me partway through. When I tried again with one page, it told me I had no tool calls left for this turn.

Since I didn't read any pages, I can't give you sourced notes. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from memory, so I've written nothing rather than guess at what Gill, Ellicott, Enduring Word or the others say.

If you send the request again, I'll make a few calls at a time instead of a big batch. I'd start with the sources most likely to give verse-by-verse coverage:

1. **Main reading:** enduringword.com (Song of Solomon 4), the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on biblehub.com, and preceptaustin.org's Song of Solomon 4 page.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon's sermons on verses 7, 12 and 16 (spurgeon.org), and pages on ligonier.org, desiringgod.org and 1517.org about whether to read the Song as an allegory of Christ and the church or as a poem about human married love.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes (netbible.org), bibleodyssey.org, and Catholic and Orthodox sources (newadvent.org, catholic.com, oca.org) on the bride as the Church or Mary, especially verses 7 and 12.

Each point will come with its URL, and I'll leave out any verse or view I can't find on those sites.
